title: Copilot Studio: Review panel shows agent readiness and policy blocks while building
notes: claim 36: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing treats the sign-in issue as a confirmed non-blocking warning, but Microsoft's text does not assign it that severity. The Maker guidance path also omits a documented section, and claims about previous behaviour and unchanged data access need narrowing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Previously blocked connectors failed late at publish, whereas this change moves their discovery earlier.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Review previously publish blocked. Opened both authoring-agent-status pages and admin-data-loss-prevention; they describe early restrictions and publish enforcement, not this historical before-and-after claim.
claims.fix: Replace 'A blocked connector no longer fails late at publish: the item is disabled with a reason' with 'A blocked connector appears disabled with a reason before a maker configures it'. In Change & support, replace 'makers who used to hit errors at publish will now ask about policy blocks earlier' with 'expect makers to ask about policy blocks while building'.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Review reports policy and readiness issues rather than replacing administrative governance or compliance reporting.
claims.quote: The Review panel doesn't replace admin-level governance or compliance reporting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sign-in-not-required issue specifically has Warning severity and therefore does not prevent publishing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio sign-in Warning Review; Copilot Studio Sign-in isn't required warning severity. Read both authoring-agent-status pages and admin-data-loss-prevention. The issue examples do not assign a severity to the sign-in issue.
claims.fix: Replace the Security & identity bullet with 'Review can surface an issue when sign-in is not required, so anyone with the link can use the agent. Warnings do not stop publishing; do not treat the Review panel as enforcement.' In At rollout, replace 'so a sign-in warning needs their attention before publishing' with 'and review any sign-in issue before publishing'. In the risk rationale, replace 'warnings such as sign-in not required' with 'warnings'. Microsoft documents the issue and the general severity rule separately at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-agent-status, not that issue's severity.
